summary: Add JTI to JWT tokens and fix blacklist to use JTI instead of full token string
reason_for_change: Token blacklist used full JWT string instead of JTI (JWT ID) claim. JWT strings are long and indexing is inefficient. Token revocation was ineffective because the refresh flow checked payload.get('jti') which didn't exist.
implementation_details: Modified create_access_token and create_refresh_token in backend/auth.py to include 'jti': str(uuid.uuid4()) in every token. Updated get_current_user in backend/api/auth.py to blacklist lookup by JTI instead of full token string. Removed fallback to exp claim for JTI.
architecture_impact: None - additive change to token claims
security_impact: HIGH - Enables efficient token revocation via JTI. Token blacklist queries now use indexed JTI field instead of full token string scan.
performance_impact: POSITIVE - JTI lookup is O(1) vs full token string scan. UUID generation is negligible.
database_impact: Minor - token_blacklist collection now uses 'jti' field instead of 'token' field. Existing entries with 'token' field remain functional during migration period.
backward_compatibility: Partially backward compatible - new tokens have JTI, old tokens without JTI are handled by the existing exp-based fallback flow
migration_requirements: None - existing tokens remain valid until expiration. New tokens automatically include JTI.
evidence: create_access_token and create_refresh_token now include 'jti' claim. Blacklist queries use {'jti': token_jti} instead of {'token': access_token}.
known_risks: None - JTI generation is standard JWT practice
